logline: A tribal dancer witnesses a murder at a Manali wedding celebration and the powerful Atwal family begins systematically hunting down everyone who saw what happened.

renewal.note: Four seasons as of May 2026. Season 4 released May 1, 2026, with the show described as its final season by some reviewers. SonyLIV's longest-running crime original.

bollymeter.basis: The Times of India gave Season 1 three-and-a-half out of five stars calling it an engrossing and gritty crime drama, and audience ratings on IMDb tracked close to 7.9, making this one of SonyLIV's best-received originals at launch.

seasons.review_body: Undekhi arrived on SonyLIV on July 10, 2020 as a crime thriller from director Ashish R Shukla. The premise is viscerally direct: a wedding in Manali, a murder in front of witnesses, and the Atwal family - politically connected and brutal - closing off every exit. The Times of India scored it 3.5 out of 5 and described it as an engrossing and gritty crime drama, a verdict that tracked the general Indian critical consensus. The show's strongest asset is Harsh Chhaya as the patriarch Papaji, a villain whose menace is structural rather than theatrical - his power derives from systems, not individual sadism. Dibyendu Bhattacharya's DSP Barun Ghosh provides the investigative counterweight. Season 1 built a loyal SonyLIV audience through consistent pacing and a believable power-dynamics framework, grounding the thriller in recognisable Indian rural-political realities.

episode_reviews.title: Episode 1
episode_reviews.spoiler_free: Undekhi's premiere drops viewers into an inciting incident of devastating specificity: a Punjabi wedding, a corrupt cop, and a crime witnessed only by the wedding's DJ from outside India. The episode establishes the series' core tension - witnesses to power who cannot safely speak - with the procedural confidence that distinguishes it from generic crime streaming.
episode_reviews.the_moment: The crime at the wedding - staged not as action spectacle but as an ordinary, quiet atrocity that the episode refuses to frame as extraordinary.
episode_reviews.review_body: Undekhi's premiere earns its 7.5 editorial score through the intelligence of its inciting incident. The setting - a lavish Punjabi wedding - and the social architecture it makes visible (wealth, police complicity, caste hierarchy) are established in the first episode without reducing any of them to symbols. Surya Sharma and Harsh Chhaya anchor the pilot's power dynamic with specific menace: one as the entitled perpetrator, one as the complicit authority figure. The South African witness Rinku (Apeksha Porwal) introduces the outsider-observer angle that the series uses to make the power structure legible to viewers without making it unfamiliar. SonyLIV crime drama at its most formally confident.

bollymeter.basis: The Times of India again gave Season 2 three-and-a-half stars, praising the solid performances and crisp script that extended the cat-and-mouse chase without collapsing the original tension.

seasons.review_body: Season 2 dropped March 4, 2022, following witnesses and investigators deeper into the Atwal family's network as the chase extends beyond Manali. The show maintains a 3.5-star endorsement from The Times of India, with solid performances and a crisp script that preserves the cat-and-mouse dynamic from Season 1. Its consistent strength, moral clarity about who holds power and why, carries through the second run, even as the narrative stretches across too many threads for the tension to stay as focused as in the first season. The ensemble, particularly Bhattacharya and Chhaya, remains the central draw.
seasons.season_over_season: Season 2 expands the geographic and political scope of the Atwal conflict but loses some of the tight, suffocating pressure of the Manali-bound original.
